name: Rochester Gas and Electric Corporation
territory: Nine-county region centred on Rochester, NY
filing_case: Case 25-E-0379 (temporary rates Jun 2026; final order pending)
_dc_note: Upstate NY data centre load estimated at ~300 MW (2026) reflecting 179% increase in requested MVA at RG&E 2022-2024 per Avangrid SCC testimony. Growth rate 5%/yr reflects projects already approved and under construction proceeding, constrained by Governor Hochul's May 2026 moratorium on new data centres over 50 MW. Source: Avangrid 'Powering New York' SCC presentation July 2025; NY Executive Order No. 62 June 2026.
_sources: Rate base, annual_capex_m and total_revenue_m are ESTIMATED, back-calculated from the June 2025 filing under NYPSC Case 25-E-0379. PSC set temporary rates June 1 2026 (+4.0% electric); final order still pending — update these figures when the final order is issued. ROE is the utility's requested rate (10.0%), not yet approved. Data centre load parameters reflect upstate NY DC siting activity.
_notes: capacity_market / capacity_market_zone are descriptive metadata pointing to shared/capacity_markets/NYISO.json; not yet consumed by the model engine at this refactoring stage — CAPACITY_COST_START remains a notebook-level global.
_class_shares_note: EIA Form 861, 2024 (Sales_Ult_Cust_2024.xlsx), Rochester Gas & Electric Corp, NY: bundled (Part A) + delivery-only (Part C) rows, so retail-choice load is included. Residential sales 2,842,349 of 6,871,716 MWh = 41.4%; residential customers 351,481 of 392,342 = 89.6%. Used only when CAPACITY_SAVINGS_ALLOCATION = 'sales_share' (CORRECTED): the residential capacity credit is scaled by sales share / customer share.

forward_assumptions._note: Forward assumptions for the layer engine (engine/layers.py). Data only for v1.0 / CORRECTED, which do not read this section. Levels: for layer assumptions, 'low' is the value that gives customers a SMALLER shared-savings effect and 'high' a LARGER one, so all-low / all-high bracket the outcome. For load-growth and price-growth assumptions (system_needs, projection, capacity price growth) 'low'/'high' mean lower/higher growth. 'derived' = computed from a cited input by the stated method; '_VERIFY' = judgement or placeholder needing a utility-specific source.

supply_energy_growth.source: Assumption: central = INFLATION_RATE (flat real energy prices); range +/-

transmission_growth.source: Assumption: central = INFLATION_RATE; high reflects transmission build-out

program_surcharge_growth.source: Assumption: BAU surcharge rates grow with inflation (policy-driven)

cost_per_mw_yr.unit: $M per MW-yr of peak reduction delivered
cost_per_mw_yr.source: Placeholder for a blended EE / electrification / DR portfolio. Anchors: Brattle Ontario (2026) $50/kW-yr DER capacity cost (high case, DR-like resources; cited in notebook Section 1 OPEX_RATIO note); Pepco Rider R-DLC pays $40-80 per controlled device per year (Pepco MD tariff p. 49). Efficiency and electrification deliver peak kW at higher cost, so central $150/kW-yr and low $300/kW-yr are judgement.

wholesale_energy.label: Hook for a later step: wholesale energy price effects

roe.label: Hook for a later step: allowed ROE

capacity_carve_out.source: Price: shared/capacity_markets/NYISO.json zone G_H_I $0.070M/MW-yr = $191.78/MW-day. Peak: RGE.json. Residential share and customers: EIA-861 2024. Scaling 1.0 (NYISO installed reserve margin not applied).
capacity_carve_out.method: Residential capacity obligation per customer = peak_mw x residential_share x obligation_scaling / residential_customers; $/month = obligation (kW) x price ($/kW-day) x 365/12. Assumes the residential share of the capacity obligation equals its share of sales; residential load is peakier, so this likely understates residential capacity. The derived amount is moved out of the parent line; the total bill is unchanged.
